transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-02
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Chen (Redwood SE), Oliver Reyes (Granite Procurement), Maya Singh (Granite Legal), Diego Alvarez (Granite CTO)

Auto-generated summary:
High-level: Triage of MSA/DPA redlines and alignment on acceptance criteria for a small production pilot. Key concerns: KMS integration, data residency, SLA credit language, and privileged keying. Next steps: Redwood to send consolidated redlines + SLA language; customer to confirm non-negotiables.

Topics:
- DPA redlines and non-negotiables
- SLA metrics and remedy/credits
- KMS and privileged keys (on-prem vs cloud KMS)
- Pilot scope and success criteria
- Pricing lanes for hosted vs dedicated

Questions raised:
- Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM in Private?
- How are egress fees calculated for high volume?
- What is rollback/fallback policy for model variants during outages?

Action items (captured):
- See metadata action_items (owners/due dates)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, can you all hear me ok?
[00:06] Oliver Reyes: Yup, loud and clear. Thanks Samir.
[00:12] Lina Chen: Heard. Got the agenda, we'll triage the redlines and then walk SLA/pricing.
[00:20] Maya Singh: Hi, sorry slight delay, joining from the west coast.
[00:24] Diego Alvarez: On our side too, afternoon all.

[01:02] Samir Patel: Cool. Oliver, real quick — what's the procurement timeline? I know you mentioned quarterly board approval, is that right?
[01:12] Oliver Reyes: Right — we need vendor acceptance into the procurement portal by mid-December to hit the Jan 15 rollout. So ideally we lock MSA/DPA by next week. Tight but doable.
[01:28] Maya Singh: We have three non-negotiables for DPA: customer-managed keys or certified HSM, 7 year audit logs retention, and a clause around model output data not being used for training.
[01:44] Lina Chen: Understood. On the KMS item, Redwood Private supports bring-your-own-KMS with HSM backed keys, and we also have dedicated keying for dedicated clusters — I can pull the technical note.
[01:58] Diego Alvarez: Quick clarifying Q — when you say "bring-your-own-KMS" does that require network peering/VPC? Or can it be an on-prem HSM endpoint?
[02:10] Lina Chen: Good question. We support both patterns. For on-prem HSM you need a private network tunnel (VPN or direct peering) for key fetch; for cloud KMS we integrate via your KMS API with client-side TLS. There are latency considerations but we've seen sub-50ms key retrieval in most configs.

[03:05] Maya Singh: The DPA wording for training is sensitive — we prefer explicit "no-training" and audit rights. The redline you sent earlier had a generic clause, we'd need it tightened.
[03:18] Samir Patel: Absolutely. We'll provide a tightened clause. Question for you: is audit rights limited to security audits or do you want broader access?
[03:28] Maya Singh: Security and privacy audits, plus the ability to request logs for specific time windows on demand.

[04:00] Oliver Reyes: On SLA, finance is pushing for credits for sustained latency breaches, not just single incident credits; how does Redwood handle progressive credits?
[04:12] Samir Patel: We can do tiered remedies. Typical we offer percentages of monthly invoice based on sustained SLO miss windows. We should capture target latency SLO (p50/p95/p99). For hosted customers you get standard SLA; for Dedicated we can negotiate tighter SLOs.
[04:30] Diego Alvarez: We need p99 <= 220ms for inference at our typical 800 token workload, is that realistic?
[04:40] Lina Chen: On dedicated GPU pools we can usually hit p99 around 180–220ms depending on batching. For hosted it depends on regional routing and bursting noise. Also note quantization and model size effects.

[05:22] Maya Singh: Another legal item: data residency. Some of our EU clients require EU-only processing.
[05:30] Samir Patel: We have region pinning and private deployments in EU regions. For Private on-prem we of course process within your infra. I'll put region clauses in the DPA/msa appendix.

[06:10] Oliver Reyes: Pricing — we have two lanes: a hosted pilot lane for quick time-to-value and a dedicated lane if we go to prod. Can you give a rough delta in unit cost?
[06:22] Samir Patel: Sure. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token and per-embedding rates; dedicated is committed capacity where unit cost drops with reserved GPU hours. Lina, do you want to call out numbers?
[06:34] Lina Chen: Example: for a medium LLM workload, hosted inference might be $0.0009 per token effective; dedicated with a 12-month commit could be ~30–40% lower unit cost, plus a fixed infra fee. We'll send spreadsheet examples.

[07:10] Diego Alvarez: Are there egress fees back to our systems? We often move embeddings out for similarity stores.
[07:18] Samir Patel: Egress is typically metered for large exports. We'll detail egress fee thresholds; for small embedding fetches under a certain volume it's negligible but for bulk exports we do apply standard bandwidth billing.

[08:05] Maya Singh: On privileged keys and escrow — we need to know how you handle key rotation and key escrow in a disaster recovery scenario.
[08:16] Lina Chen: Key rotation is customer-managed in BYOK; for private deployments we support HSM-backed rotation policies and we can provide a sealed escrow process under an escrow agreement if needed.

[09:02] Samir Patel: Ok let's walk through the most material redlines you sent (Maya). Can you summarize the top five?
[09:12] Maya Singh: Sure — 1) No-training language tightened, 2) Audit rights and log retention to seven years, 3) Customer-managed KMS or HSM support, 4) Data residency and subprocessors list updated, 5) SLA remedy escalation for sustained misses.
[09:30] Samir Patel: Thanks. We'll accept items 1,3 provisionally and propose tightened language for 2,4,5 to make them operationally reasonable.

[10:05] Oliver Reyes: For the SLA remedy, finance wants an automated credit calculation so it's auditable.
[10:12] Samir Patel: We can provide a sample formula using aggregated p99 windows over a 30-day period, and produce automatic credit calculations in the billing export.

[11:00] Diego Alvarez: We want a canary/fallback policy if the primary model has a regression — how do rollbacks happen?
[11:08] Lina Chen: Our rollout system supports canary percentages and automated fallback to previous pinned versions. For Hosted we can tie routing to policy names; for Dedicated you can pin specific variants. Note that KV cache priming may affect latency on rollbacks.
[11:25] Diego Alvarez: That "KV cache" got transcribed once as "kay vee" in our internal notes — ha — just flagging.

[12:00] Maya Singh: A procedural Q: if we need a change to the DPA, who's the signatory on Redwood side?
[12:08] Samir Patel: For most customers the legal team (I will copy our GC) signs the final DPA alongside the AE. I'll include GC contact in the redline package.

[12:45] Oliver Reyes: Can we get a short security package for procurement: SOC2 summary, penetration test cadence, and endpoint inventory?
[12:55] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll attach the security pack. We have SOC 2 Type II and regular pentest summaries.

[13:30] Maya Singh: On model output usage: we need an explicit clause that prevents Redwood from using our content for model training and a notification clause for any new subprocessors.
[13:40] Samir Patel: We'll add explicit wording and a subprocessors appendix with notification windows for changes.

[14:20] Lina Chen: One operational note on the KMS path — if you go with an on-prem HSM, there will be an additional latency hop on key unwrap; we typically recommend asymmetric operations cached at the host. We'll include a diagram.

[15:02] Diego Alvarez: Is there a template for the network topology you need? Our infra team will want to review.
[15:09] Lina Chen: Yes, I'll send a PDF with example VPC peering and prov tunnels. That will include ports and IP ranges.

[16:00] Oliver Reyes: Regarding pilot sizing: we want a 4-week pilot for 50k requests/day, with a canary ramp. What SLA do we expect for that pilot?
[16:12] Samir Patel: For pilot we can set a best-effort SLO with a target p99 under 350ms for hosted; if you pick Dedicated pilot we can aim for p99 under 250ms. Pilot pricing will be discounted as a trial; we'll outline the delta in the spreadsheet.

[17:05] Maya Singh: One more redline concern — indemnity carveouts for data exfiltration need to be symmetric. We submitted language.
[17:14] Samir Patel: We'll have legal review that and propose mutual carveouts where feasible.

[18:00] Oliver Reyes: If we accept the MSA redlines with the exceptions you propose, can you get the revised DPA back to us by Monday EOD?
[18:08] Samir Patel: We'll aim for Monday EOD. That aligns with the procurement window.

[19:00] Lina Chen: Quick follow: for the pilot, if you want us to run a short benchmark against your sample prompts, we can schedule a 2-hour run and provide a latency/cost report.
[19:10] Diego Alvarez: Yes please — that would be useful.

[20:02] Maya Singh: About service credits: we need a cap on total credits per incident and per month — that's standard for us.
[20:12] Samir Patel: We can include a cap; usually it's a percentage of monthly fees. We'll propose language.

[21:00] Oliver Reyes: Any competitors we should be aware of? Our committee mentioned BigCloudAI and NimbusServe. How do you compare on private deployments?
[21:10] Samir Patel: Compared to BigCloudAI, we offer more opinionated inference runtime and easier private deployment with transparent performance profiles. NimbusServe has flexible ops but we often beat them on unit cost at scale. We'll provide a short comparison doc.

[22:05] Maya Singh: Operational checklist — do you support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for RBAC by default?
[22:13] Lina Chen: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM are supported for Enterprise plans and included in Dedicated and Private deployments.

[23:00] Diego Alvarez: On data retention — seven years is long. Can we scope it by data class and include purging workflows?
[23:10] Maya Singh: We prefer specific classes retained longer, but some logs we want kept for compliance. We'll provide a class list.

[24:00] Samir Patel: Ok let's recap next steps and owners quickly.
[24:06] Samir Patel: Action items — Samir to consolidate redlines and send proposed DPA + SLA language by 2027-12-06. Lina to send topology PDF and pilot benchmark template by 2027-12-08. Maya to send final non-negotiables by 2027-12-05.
[24:30] Oliver Reyes: We'll review and aim to have procurement board sign-off by mid-December.

[25:10] Maya Singh: A scheduling note — if legal needs a short follow-up, can we do a 30-min readout next Wednesday?
[25:18] Samir Patel: Yes, I'll set a 30-min slot.

[26:00] Diego Alvarez: Minor: please include model explainability notes; our compliance team will want them.
[26:07] Lina Chen: We'll include a summary of explainability features and eval harness results.

[27:00] Oliver Reyes: Any last concerns?
[27:06] Maya Singh: Not from legal; main thing is to get the tightened DPA language.
[27:10] Diego Alvarez: No further technical questions.

[28:00] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs. Expect the consolidated packet Monday.
[28:10] Oliver Reyes: Great, thanks.
[28:15] Maya Singh: Thanks all.
[28:18] Diego Alvarez: Thanks.

[47:50] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: some product names were transcribed variably (e.g., Redwood Dedicated as "Redwood Dedicate"), and internal acronyms (KV cache) occasionally spelled out. Please rely on the attachments for canonical docs.
